_source: CLAUDE.md §46 REPRODUCIBILITY and §47 SYSTEM VERSIONING. The nine reproducibility items and the thirteen version-significant change kinds below are the spec's own lists, in its order and wording. scripts/tests/test_versioning.py parses them back out of CLAUDE.md.
_why_one_file: §46 asks what makes a result reproducible; §47 asks what makes a system a different system. They are the same question asked of a result and of the thing that produced it, and the Trading System version is an item in BOTH lists. One registry so that version cannot mean two things.

reproducibility._spec: CLAUDE.md §46: 'A result without reproducibility metadata must not be treated as equivalent to a fully reproducible experiment.'

items.definition: The git commit, AND whether the tree was dirty. A dirty tree means the commit does not identify the code that ran, so 'commit abc123' alone is not a capture -- it is a guess with a hash attached.
Which version of the system produced the result (§47). Shared with the versioning half of this file on purpose.
§11's record of the configuration, by value.

Which providers answered, in which role, and what each declared it could do at the time (§6). A result computed while a provider was degraded is a different result, and nothing else in the capture list would show it.

The seed of every stochastic step. `null` is acceptable ONLY with an explicit statement that nothing stochastic ran -- since §39 and §45 added bootstraps and Monte Carlo, that statement is no longer true by default.
The values the run used, by value.
In-sample, out-of-sample and holdout ranges, named separately (§44).
What §45 concluded, INCLUDING the checks that did not run. A result whose validation state is 'NOT_RUN on six of eleven checks' is reproducible and unvalidated, and those are different facts.

grades.PARTIAL: some items captured; the result can be described but not re-run identically

reproducibility._not_equivalent: §46's last sentence is a rule about COMPARISON, which is where the harm happens: a fully reproducible result and a partial one placed in the same ranking table are treated as equivalent by the reader whatever the footnote says. scripts/versioning.py compare() refuses to return a comparison without both grades attached, and `assert_comparable()` raises when the grades differ.

versioning._spec: CLAUDE.md §47: canonical Trading System versioning v1, v2, v3 ... 'Do not create a separate incompatible AI strategy version system.'

grammar._note: A candidate is v<parent>.<n> so its parent is readable from its own name -- §47's example is exactly 'Trading System v1 -> Candidate v1.x -> Approved Trading System v2'. There is no third form: a change that is not a released version or a candidate for one has nowhere to live, which is the point.

versioning._all_are_significant: All thirteen are version-significant. §47 calls them 'examples', which is a floor and not a ceiling: an unlisted change may also be significant, so `is_significant()` takes a declared kind OR an explicit argument, and there is no way to declare a listed kind insignificant.
versioning._rejected_candidates: §47: 'Rejected candidates must remain traceable.' A rejected candidate keeps its version number forever -- v1.3 is never reissued to a different candidate. `next_candidate()` therefore reads the §42 experiment store, not a counter, so a number that was spent on something rejected stays spent.
